summary: Track C C4 completed: tree surgery in `probes/lemma612-scaffold.lean` (extended in place, not a new file -- the choice left open by C3's dispatch). `star` FIXED from a double-`bigAnd` (`(bigAnd labels).and(bigAnd children)`) to a single `bigAnd` over the concatenated list (labels ++ children-diamonds) -- verified by hand BEFORE editing that the old version fails Simpson's own worked-example check (produces a spurious `top.and(dia(top.and top))` instead of the source's plain `dia top` at a label-less, single-childed node). `prune`/`fullSubtree` added (children split `pre ++ [c]`, continuation child LAST, matching `addChild`'s pre-existing append-at-end convention -- chosen to stay consistent with what C5's `addChild`/`pathSpine` commutation lemma will need). The unfolding identity (report 02 section 2.3, `Gamma@(fullSubtree v) = Gamma@(prune v c) AND dia(Gamma@(fullSubtree c))`) is proved as a genuine IK-derivable TWO-WAY IMPLICATION (`star_unfold_imp1`/`star_unfold_imp2`), NOT as a raw Lean `Eq`: `bigAnd`'s own right-fold definition (`phi::rest => phi.and(bigAnd rest)`) makes literal term equality fail once the pruned node has 2+ ordinary children (associativity mismatch between `a.and(X.and y)` and `(a.and X).and y` as TERMS, despite being logically equivalent) -- this was checked by hand before writing any Lean, avoiding a dead-end attempt at an unprovable `rfl` statement. Built via new reusable infrastructure, all generic over the axiom set: `andI_deriv`/`andE1_deriv`/`andE2_deriv` (AndI/AndE1/AndE2 lifted to an arbitrary Deriv-context), `top_deriv` (top is derivable in any context), `bigAnd_cons_of_ne_nil` (bigAnd's cons-equation for a propositionally-nonempty tail), and the algebraic core `bigAnd_append_singleton_imp1`/`imp2` (pulling the last conjunct out of bigAnd's scope, by induction on the list). The plan's explicitly-flagged-defective `pathTo`/`pathToList` (mutual recursion, returned the FULL not pruned subtree) and `Star_append` (wrapped the appended tree in its full star, the wrong primitive for the pruning problem) were DELETED. The success criterion (report 02's C4 entry: reproduce Simpson's worked example verbatim, tree x->y and x->z->w, target z) was investigated and found to NOT be achievable via literal `#eval`/`decide`: `Label Atom` has no `deriving DecidableEq` anywhere in the codebase, and the file's only decidability source is the classically-opaque `Classical.propDecidable` local instance, so `Gamma.filter (fun x => x.lbl = l)` does not computationally reduce. Verified this diagnosis with a standalone scratch probe (confirming `simp` with a supplied inequality proof still closes such filter goals regardless of instance opacity) before committing to the approach: `star_Star_worked_example` states and proves the exact target formula as a genuine `Eq` via `simp`-driven unfolding, not `rfl`/`decide`. Landed sorry-free, axiom footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` on all five new top-level theorems (`star_unfold_imp1`, `star_unfold_imp2`, `star_Star_worked_example`, `bigAnd_append_singleton_imp1`, `bigAnd_append_singleton_imp2`) -- no new axioms. `Star`/`Star_imp1`/`Star_imp2`/`box_mono1`/`box_mono2`/`IK.impIntro`/`NIKAx`/`TClosure.hilbertTransport` all unchanged (they reference `star Gamma t` only opaquely, never unfold its equation, so were not at regression risk from the `star` fix) and reverified compiling. `probes/track-c-c1-tele-conj.lean` (C1/C2/C3) untouched, reverified compiling. No `Cslib/` file touched. Per the explicit HARD STOP instruction, C5 was NOT opened this dispatch.
